key_insight: A neural topology-optimization method using a convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KATO) can design ship structures that lower forced-vibration active input power while avoiding the resonance-pathology issues of standard dynamic compliance objectives.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to quieter, more fatigue-resistant ship decks and foundations with controlled feature sizes, manufacturability, and improved static performance after extrusion.
method: Optimize ship structures with active input power (AIP) as the vibration objective
Use KATO with Helmholtz filtering and Heaviside projection for feature-size and tolerance control
Compare against GCMMA on deck-panel and thruster-foundation cases, including unrestricted, manufacturing-aware, stress-aware, and near-resonant designs
evidence_signal: Across both design families, all optimized layouts reduced AIP versus size-optimized references; KATO matched GCMMA within 0.5 dB in AIP, achieved 22–36x lower binary static compliance in frame variants, and ran 6.4–10.4x faster in stress-aware formulations.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen filtering/projection, finite-depth extrusion, and problem setup, so performance and speed may change when applied to different ship geometries, load cases, or manufacturing constraints.
paper_title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
